what: ATI makes specialty materials: titanium, nickel-based superalloys and specialty steels used in jet engines, airframes, medical implants and energy equipment. Aerospace and defence are its largest markets.
customers: Jet engine and airframe manufacturers, defence contractors, medical device makers and energy companies.
money: titanium and nickel alloys, forgings and castings for aerospace
specialty stainless and precision rolled strip
moat: Melting and forging capacity qualified into jet engine programmes, where approval takes years and engine makers cannot easily switch supplier mid-programme.
risks: Aerospace build rates depend on Boeing and Airbus delivery schedules
Nickel and titanium input costs are volatile
opportunities: Revenue grew about 5% last year with a return on invested capital of 14%
Analysts see about 37% upside from current levels
Jet engine build and spare part demand is in a multi-year upcycle
watch: Aerospace and defence revenue share and jet engine order rates.
